newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car sales fall for second consecutive month.
newsitem.headline: Japan car sales fall for second consecutive month.

text.p: Car sales in Japan fell in May for the second consecutive month as a sales tax increase continued to dull consumers' appetite for new cars, an industry body said Monday.
Vehicle sales, including cars, trucks and buses, fell 9.4 percent in May from a year earlier to 319,940 units, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said.
The drop followed a decline of 12.7 percent in April, after Japan's consumption tax rose to 5 percent from 3 percent April 1.
Domestic sales in May by Toyota Motor Corp., Japan's top carmaker, fell 8.1 percent year-on-year to 126,996 units, after a 15.7 percent drop in April.
Sales of imported vehicles fell 27.0 percent in May to 22,921 units after a huge 36.8 percent decline in April.
Imported car sales in particular are struggling because they are generally more expensive than Japanese cars, the association official said.
Domestic sales by Honda Motor Co. Ltd fell a sharp 14.8 percent in May to 34,762 units after declining just 1.6 percent in April, the company's first fall in 26 months.

"Orders recovered in the middle of May to the same level as last May, but it was tough to post a gain as sales in May last year were high due to strong demand for our recreation vehicles," a Honda spokesman said.

The only one of Japan's five big carmakers to post an increase in domestic sales last month was Mazda Motor Corp., whose sales climbed by 12.7 percent to 20,539 units, after falling 9.9 percent in April.
Sales by Nissan Motor Co. Ltd, Japan's second-biggest carmaker, fell 12.4 percent to 59,361 units in May after a 5.3 percent decline in April.
Mitsubishi Motors Corp.'s sales fell 10.6 percent to 25,549 units in May, an improvement from April's 24.7 percent drop.
